summary: Authoritative game-server SDKs for multiplayer rooms, available in Node.js/TypeScript, Go, Rust, C#, and C++. They share the Room Host Protocol v1. The browser-only @randseed/game-sdk is a separate client package.

node.heading: Node.js SDK (GitHub)
node.installGuidance: Pin a reviewed tag or commit instead of main for reproducible builds.
node.requirements: Target fixed runtime nodejs-22 or nodejs-24 in randseed.fullstack.json and bundle the room server into a single ESM entrypoint for code.tar.gz.

capabilities.name: Authoritative multiplayer
capabilities.description: A shared match lifecycle for initialization, ticks, player joins and leaves, trusted room commands, and terminal results.

capabilities.name: Room player limits
capabilities.description: Configure integers with 1 <= minPlayers <= maxPlayers <= 100. minPlayers counts assigned players, not connected WebSockets; maxPlayers is seat capacity, not a fill target. Set both equal for a fixed-size roster.

capabilities.name: Room client migration
capabilities.description: For the startup and first-observation rollout, use browser @randseed/game-sdk 0.4.0 or a compatible later release once published; rebuild and redeploy room games. The browser SDK handles acknowledgement; no server SDK upgrade is required for this rollout.

capabilities.name: Session recovery
capabilities.description: Node.js and Rust support Session Stream v1 with checkpoint hydration, contiguous ticks, deterministic replay, and action results. Keep seats, hands, turns, and timers in authoritative state so a reconnect can recover the current match.

capabilities.name: Disconnect behavior
capabilities.description: A leave can be a temporary disconnect and a join can be a reconnect. Implement seat retention, waiting, timeouts, and forfeits in game rules; the server SDK does not configure a general per-player disconnect wait.

capabilities.name: Private player views
capabilities.description: Node.js and Rust validate recipient-specific views against the active roster and fail closed instead of exposing canonical state.

capabilities.name: Match results
capabilities.description: Versioned Result Units represent round, stage, team, participant, and match outcomes with declared metrics.

capabilities.name: Structured failures
capabilities.description: Node.js and Rust report stable error codes, retryability, and sanitized callback failures.

capabilities.name: Agent integration
capabilities.description: Optional Node.js and Rust interfaces expose Agent capabilities and trusted, recipient-specific player views.

capabilities.name: Room services
capabilities.description: Node.js and Rust PlatformClient APIs provide host-mediated SQL, key-value storage, broadcasts, direct messages, and online player profiles.

routes.name: GET /manifest
routes.description: Game metadata, options schema, player-view mode, and Result Unit definitions.

routes.name: POST /init
routes.description: Initialize a match from host-provided players and options.

routes.name: POST /tick
routes.description: Apply one authoritative tick of player inputs and commands.

routes.name: POST /onPlayerJoin
routes.description: Handle a player joining or reconnecting without duplicating an existing seat.

routes.name: POST /onPlayerLeave
routes.description: Handle a player disconnecting or leaving according to the game's offline rules; no disconnect reason is supplied.

routes.name: POST /isGameOver
routes.description: Return terminal status, match summary, and next-match policy.

routes.name: WebSocket /stream
routes.description: Exchange hydrate and step messages for stateful simulation, recovery, replay, and action results.

routes.name: GET /agent/capabilities
routes.description: Declare supported Agent protocols and control modes.

routes.name: GET /agent/player-contract
routes.description: Declare per-seat view and action schemas.

routes.name: POST /agent/player-view
routes.description: Project a recipient-only view for the trusted room host.
